claim: The 2026-10-05 frozen scheduled IBKR paper read-only run passed through the official ibapi 10.45.1 client and NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 HistoricalInteractiveBrokersClient. The official receipt reports one DU-prefix paper account, zero positions/open orders, REALTIME SPY contract/quote data and zero noninformational errors; the native adapter resolved SPY.ARCA and returned five daily bars and 390 five-minute bars. Native process exit 0 and terminal strong_native_postcheck exit 0 corroborate clean completion of this bounded read-only sequence.

limitations: Read-only step 1 only. No order submission, cancellation, fill, flatten, kill-switch or execution-adapter qualification is established; the ibkr-local-acceptance gate remains not_established.
No NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 recovery or reconnect/restart reconciliation was exercised; #5007, #5057 and #5060 remain separate open upstream issues as checked 2026-10-05.

Paper scope is the official managed-account DU-prefix check for one account on the same loopback endpoint; no exact account-identity proof is published. The Nautilus historical client relies on the fresh official receipt and does not independently query account scope.

Zero errors means the official receipt's empty noninformational error array and no reported native instrument/bar/error fields; this does not establish visibility into every native callback or log error.
Quote age -0.190 s is retained unchanged. The probe uses IB server/last-trade times at one-second resolution and permits a -2 s lower bound; server-minus-local delta is -1.008 s.
The Gateway image digest and read-only mode are bound compose configuration; the supplied run artifacts do not include an independent runtime container-image inspection or an API write-refusal trial.
This is one bounded session. Actual wire-request count and provider usage remain unknown; no continuous operation, later-session, live-trading or profitability claim is made.
Private frozen wrapper/checker bytes and raw outputs are retained by their hashes; public projections and repository validation are structural publication evidence, not a new broker or model run.
